  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Given extreme right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81) and variance heterogeneity likely across paradigms, log-transformation or inverse transformation should be applied before ANOVA. Alternatively, use Welch's ANOVA for unequal variances.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean=0.73. Standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or Cochran's Q test if repeated measures structure exists. Report odds ratios relative to Sham.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with caution. Extreme right skew (max=29.82, mean=0.47) and presence of values >>1 suggest possible calculation artifacts or outliers. Winsorize or apply robust transformation (log1p) before ANOVA. Consider non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis as primary analysis.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Distribution appears more symmetric than other variables, but verify homogeneity of variance. Welch's ANOVA if variance inequality detected.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA. Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Arcsine-square-root transformation may stabilize variance near boundaries. Alternatively, beta regression for proper bounded support."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: 76,655 trials from 8 mice with unbalanced design (Combined n=48,846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3,323). Must account for mouse-level clustering via mixed-effects models or treat Mouse as blocking/random factor to avoid pseudoreplication.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each response. Expected failures for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency due to extreme tails.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's or Bartlett's test across paradigms. Expected violation given vastly different sample sizes and paradigm characteristics.",
    "For Success (binary): No normality assumption, but check for separation or quasi-complete separation in logistic regression.",
    "For AD: Check boundary effects—values near 0 or 1 may cause heteroscedasticity.",
    "Outliers: Identify extreme values in Path Efficiency (>5 or >10) and Time-to-Target (>20s) for potential data quality issues."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA or equivalent significant (p<0.05), perform pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for continuous responses meeting assumptions, or Games-Howell for unequal variances.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni-Holm correction for 10 comparisons.",
    "For Kruskal-Wallis on Path Efficiency: Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction.",
    "Priority contrasts: Combined vs each unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to test multisensory enhancement; all active vs Sham to test stimulation efficacy; ICMS Only vs Visual Only modalities to compare sensory channel efficacy.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables, Cramer's V or odds ratios for Success."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined likely shows superior performance: fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, highest Path Efficiency, and lowest AD (tightest angular control), based on typical multisensory integration benefits.",
    "ICMS Only likely outperforms visual-only conditions given direct cortical engagement, potentially showing intermediate performance between Combined and unimodal visual.",
    "Dim Visual Only and Bright Visual Only may differ: Dim condition may show degraded performance (slower, more errors, higher AD) compared to Bright, or possibly no difference if visual contrast above detection threshold in both.",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: slowest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency, highest AD, serving as baseline.",
    "Average Speed may show less paradigm differentiation than accuracy/efficiency metrics, or may trade off with Success (speed-accuracy tradeoff).",
    "Large sample size imbalance (Combined 63.7% of data) will drive statistical power; small n in Bright Visual Only (n=3,323) and Sham (n=3,505) limits precise estimation for those conditions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance across stimulation paradigms: Combined (48,846 trials) vs Bright Visual Only (3,323 trials) creates 14.7:1 ratio, reducing power for underrepresented conditions and complicating variance estimation.",
    "Multiple trials per mouse (unbalanced across mice: SC21LM 10,986 vs SC11LM 7,233) create non-independence; standard ANOVA violates independence assumption. Mixed-effects models required for valid inference.",
    "Path Efficiency distribution highly abnormal with extreme outliers (max=29.82 when theoretical maximum is 1.0), suggesting calculation errors or data quality issues that must be resolved before analysis.",
    "Success as binary outcome precludes standard ANOVA; analysis plan requires fundamentally different statistical framework.",
    "No information on trial temporal structure, learning effects, or session effects that may confound paradigm comparisons.",
    "Single dataset snapshot without replication or cross-validation for generalization.",
    "Temperature=0.5 and prompt template specifications suggest this analysis may be LLM-generated; human statistical review essential."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) or generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs) with Mouse as random intercept, Stim Paradigm as fixed effect, and appropriate family/link for each response: Gaussian with log-link for Time-to-Target, binomial logit for Success, Gaussian with log-link or beta regression for Path Efficiency, Gaussian identity for Average Speed, and beta regression or arcsine-transformed Gaussian for AD. Include random slope for Paradigm by Mouse if sufficient data. Compare models via likelihood ratio tests and report marginal means with confidence intervals."
}
